Here's a breakdown of the pattern:

* `\b`: Word boundary (ensures we match a whole email address)
* `[a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+`: Matches one or more characters that are letters (both uppercase and lowercase), numbers, dot (.), hyphen (-), underscore (_), percent (%), or plus sign (+)
* `@`: Matches the @ symbol
* `[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+`: Matches one or more characters that are letters (both uppercase and lowercase), numbers, dot (.), or hyphen (-)
* `\.`: Matches a period (.) character
* `[a-zA-Z]{2,}`: Matches the domain extension (it must be at least 2 characters long)
* `\b`: Word boundary (ensures we match a whole email address)

You can use this regular expression in your favorite programming language or text editor to extract all email addresses from the text.
